I agree with pretty much everything you said. That being said, I'm leaving the career as an SWE too. My company flat out told us they no longer want the engineering team to code; that we should only be using AI to code because "any manual coding is inefficient and a waste of time". And they paired that with announcing that they now require over 2x the amount of sprint work per engineer per sprint, encouraging us to use AI to get it done. All at the same time they did more layoffs. They laid off the entire UI/UX design team, and replaced them with an AI tool. Over half of the company has been laid off within the last year alone. I have several friends in similar situations. Some are still fighting to keep their jobs, two were just got laid off within the last month, and two more have been searching for jobs since earlier this year with no luck. Being an SWE has been a huge blessing. But the job market sucks right now and it seems to be getting worse. The people who get to decide whether I have a job or not have already been acting on their belief that AI can fully replace us (hence the many layoffs at my and my friends' workplaces). Hopefully it all irons out, but I personally don't want to sit around waiting and hoping that the tech CEOs once again see the worth of SWEs. So while I agree with everything you said, I'm still out.

I am a software engineer with over a decade of experience working at major corporation such as Berkshire Hathaway, down to small Inc. 5000 that were crushing a niche market. I lost my job in one of the many layoffs that started in 2023. I have been unable to find developer work in California, back end, front end, full stack, it doesn't matter. What went from a nonstop stream of emails and calls from recruiters looking to fill open roles, has come to a complete silence. It's no secret that the developer job market is completely wrecked right now. There are going to be growing pains. The total amount of roles has been reduced dramatically. That's also compounded by the fact that speculation heavily drives the market. The good thing is that it's becoming more apparent that at the current rate, building and maintaining applications with frontier AI will be cost prohibitive. The other side to that sword is that open source models continue to get better and running local models may be feasible at frontier level capacity. This video should be titled, "Will current AI take your job" and yes the answer to that is no. The thing you fail to realize is that every advancement in technology, every automation, was for a narrow domain. The systems we are trying to build are general. We see it to some extent with the AI we already have, they are far more general than anything we have built previously. The problem comes when you have a system that can generalize to any domain, like humans do. At that point this will no longer be a tool, any leverage you have is gone. Now you might say "Well who cares, then its like we have our own super human to do our each and every whim". Well yes, this is true, but this assumes that this AGI will be aligned to our values, that they have a exceptionally robust understanding of what we want and desire, and acts only our goals and not their proxied assumption of our goals. This is the alignment problem, and we do not know how to solve it. Not to mention that even if everyone had a AGI in their pocket that did exactly what they wanted, the implications is so mind bogglingly complex that its about the same as everyone having a nuke. To summarize as to what this video misses completely. 1) Narrow AI/Automation will never take our jobs general AI can (if we allow it i.e. if the compliance surrounding having a human around is forgone). 2) Aligning AI is an unsolved problem so if we do get AGI we don't know what goals it will choose to achieve. 3) Even if we have aligned AGI the implications on any human having it is so complex and convoluted that it would require us solving a mountain of problems we haven't got the slightest awareness about. 4) The rate of progress is moving far too quickly and we aren't able to keep up with the change fast enough to figure out how to control any of these systems before they are integrated into every facet of our lives. 5) Integration of increasingly more powerful AI is currently occurring faster than we understand them and is leading to a gradual disempowerment scenario, where our ability to steer what happens in the world is diminishing.
